title: Primes with equal binary and ternary digit sums
credit: QED original (archived Nov 2026, restored after re-review).
plain: Show that there are infinitely many primes whose binary digit sum equals their ternary digit sum.
math: Let $s_q(n)$ be the sum of the base-$q$ digits of $n$. Prove that there are infinitely many primes $p$ with $s_2(p)=s_3(p)$. (Stronger target: $\#\{p\le N:s_2(p)=s_3(p)\}\ge N^{c}$ for some $c>0$; heuristically the count is $N^{\log3/\log4+o(1)}$-type up to the $1/\log N$ prime density.)
